decisions.reason: Changing the Topic field label to the Danish text "tema" does not resolve or alter the separate requirement for Danish as the document default language.
The source establishes the text of one localized field label but does not change the candidate's label coverage, uniqueness, help-text relationship, or persistence behavior.
The localized Topic label does not change when or how placeholder text clears upon field activation.
The Topic-to-tema localization has no effect on bullet size, appearance, alignment, scaling, or color.
Specifying one field's Danish label does not change the implementation mechanism or robustness requirements for editable fields.
The source changes user-facing field text, not the required source style system or style-catalog coverage.
The source provides a Danish alias for Topic but does not change the required alignment relationship among Item and Title, Topic, Proposal, and Start Time.
Renaming Topic to "tema" does not change the requirement that inserting a row after that field must not create an extra border.
The field-label translation does not affect hard-return spacing for continuous paragraph text.
The word "tema" is the Danish label for Topic here and does not refer to or modify the Word theme color palette.
The Topic field translation does not change the fixed-margin or pencil-icon visibility requirements in the Guidance template.
A specific user-facing field-label translation does not change the naming convention, prefix, or language of Word style names.
